Note: Precertification may be required for select procedures and interventions. Use the CPT code search tool to see if precertification is required. Medical Necessity Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved total knee arthroplasty (TKA) prosthesis is considered medically necessary for adult members when the following criteria are met (see also Additional Note ): Member has advanced joint disease demonstrated by: Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs from injury due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination: and Member has any of the following: Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis of knee joint (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) (see Appendix ); or Radiographic evidence of avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis) of tibial or femoral condyle; or Radiographic evidence or rheumatoid arthritis (joint space narrowing); and History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/body mass index (BMI)) that is clearly addressed in the medical record (see Footnote1 Note* ).
